content: The assessment of albuminuria is conducted by measuring the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), which is typically obtained from a spot urine sample. UACR levels are used to evaluate kidney function and are categorized as follows: normal levels are defined as less than 30 mg/g, moderately elevated levels range from 30 to 300 mg/g, and severely elevated levels are 300 mg/g or higher. Due to the variability in UACR measurements, it is recommended to confirm the diagnosis with two or three abnormal readings taken over a period of 3 to 6 months. The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is calculated using serum creatinine levels and is adjusted for factors such as age and other individual characteristics. Screening for both UACR and eGFR provides a comprehensive evaluation of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression.
